public.pressSubheadline: After months of work, Voldby Bio is ready – premiering with Avatar in full Dolby Atmos
public.pressIntro:
Voldby – After many months of intense work, the wait is finally over. This week, Voldby Bio opens its doors in Voldby, giving the town a brand-new destination for film lovers and cinema experiences.

Behind the opening lies extensive groundwork, with Lis and Jan — along with their dedicated helpers, including Kurth and Mads — having worked tirelessly for months. Premises had to be found, plans drawn up, the auditorium built, and the technology installed. Every single detail, from seat comfort to room acoustics, has been carefully planned to create the best possible film experience.

The result is a modern cinema where both picture and sound are absolutely top-class.

Special focus has been placed on the sound. The main auditorium is fitted with an advanced Dolby Atmos sound system, where audio can move freely around the room to create a more realistic and immersive experience for the audience. With speakers positioned both around and above the audience, sound is placed precisely in the room, so guests feel right in the middle of the film's world.
public.pressPremiere:
And what film could be more fitting to inaugurate the new setup than one of the world's biggest box-office hits?

The opening programme therefore features the spectacular blockbuster Avatar, whose stunning visual effects and sweeping soundtrack were made for the big screen.

As the lights dim, the screen lights up, and the first notes from the world of Pandora fill the room, it also marks the starting shot for a new era of cinema experiences in Voldby.
public.pressClosing:
For the owner of Voldby Bio, the opening is the culmination of a long journey. From the first ideas and drawings to the installation of the picture and sound systems, the project has demanded patience, passion, and countless hours of work.

Now, everything is ready.

And when the first guests settle into their seats, it won't just be a film premiere — but also the beginning of a new gathering place for film-loving residents of Voldby.

The magic of cinema is back — bigger and more spectacular than ever.
public.press2Headline: Now the cinema guests decide for themselves
public.press2Subheadline: A new voting feature and smart email updates make it easier than ever to keep up with Voldby Bio
public.press2Intro:
Voldby — Voldby Bio's online portal has gained a number of new features that give the cinema's regular guests more say in what gets shown — and better notice when something happens.

The biggest news is a new voting feature. From now on, guests can request a film for screening, after which Jan gathers the best suggestions and lets the household vote on which one gets shown next.
public.press2Heading1: Vote on the next movie night
public.press2Body1:
The voting works simply: a guest requests a film for screening, and once enough good suggestions have come in, they're put to a vote. Everyone can then vote for their favourite, and the result can be followed as the votes come in.

When the poll closes, the winner is scheduled as a real movie night on the calendar — and everyone who voted automatically gets notified once it's set.
public.press2Heading2: Prettier messages — and a bit of practical tidying
public.press2Body2:
At the same time, the portal has gained a whole new messaging system. Get a reply to a wish or a screening request, and it now also lands in your inbox as a real email with a film poster and a few words — not just as a message inside the portal.

This does require setting your email address in Settings, though. It only takes a moment, and then you won't miss the next round of news from Voldby Bio either.

And should you forget your password along the way, there's help at hand now too: you can reset it yourself, without waiting for outside help.

public.press2EmailImageAlt: Screenshot of a new email notification with a film poster and a message about a scheduled screening

cardSize.heading: Card size
cardSize.description: Controls the size of the movie/TV show cards on the Movies and TV Shows tabs. One shared setting for both tabs.
theme.heading: Theme
theme.description: Sets a light or dark theme across the whole interface. Saved to your account, so it follows you regardless of which device you log in from. Nothing chosen follows your device's own setting automatically.
sync.movieDescription: Fetches fresh metadata (title, year, poster, plot, genres, cast, rating, runtime) from TMDb for every movie created via TMDb, and updates the locally stored copy. It does not touch your own details (tags, format, audio type, location, owner, serial number). May take a moment depending on the number of movies.
sync.tvDescription: Fetches fresh metadata (name, year, status, poster, plot, genres, cast, rating, season/episode counts) from TMDb for every TV show created via TMDb. It does not touch your own details (tags, format, location, owner, serial number), nor which seasons you own and which episodes you have watched.
sync.tvButton: Update all TV shows from TMDb
sync.abortedNoToken: Sync aborted — check that the backend has a valid TMDB_API_TOKEN.
sync.rateLimited: {synced} of {total} {items} updated, but stopped early because TMDb hit a rate limit. Try again shortly to update the rest.
libBackup.heading: Library export / restore
libBackup.description: Export the entire movie/TV library as a JSON file — to use in another system, or as a way back if the library gets messed up. This is not a full system backup (see below) — only the movie/TV data itself.
libBackup.restoreDescription: Restore replaces the entire current movie/TV library with the contents of a previously exported file — anything not in the file disappears. Choose a file and type GENDAN to confirm.
sysBackup.heading: Full system backup
sysBackup.description: Takes a full low-level backup of the whole system (movies, TV shows, deleted movies/shows, tags, users, counters) — for disaster recovery. Note: your external API keys (TMDb/UPC/Discogs/OMDb/Plex) are not included in the backup and must be re-entered manually under "System settings" below after a restore.
sysBackup.restoreDescription: Restore entire system replaces everything above with the contents of a previous system backup — including user accounts. Choose a file and type GENDAN SYSTEM to confirm.
reset.heading: Reset database
reset.description: Empties the movie/TV library completely (movies, TV shows, deleted movies/shows, tags, serial-number counters, plus Voldby BIO screenings/requests) back to an empty state. Does not touch user accounts or system settings. Irreversible — take a full system backup above first if you want to be able to undo. Confirm with your own password.
reset.done: Reset: {movies} movies, {shows} TV shows and related data removed.
cert.heading: TLS certificate
cert.description: Controls the production HTTPS certificate (Caddy, movie.ll.lan, see DEPLOYMENT.md/BUGS.md #23). Higher risk than the app's other tools — a wrong installation can make the site unreachable over HTTPS. Only meaningful in production.
cert.none: No certificate found (neither installed nor staged).
cert.method1Description: Generates a new key + CSR for external signing (e.g. via your internal CA). The key never leaves the server.
cert.pasteSignedLabel: Paste the signed certificate (PEM) once you have had the CSR signed
cert.method2Description: Alternative to the CSR flow — upload a finished .pfx/.p12 file (cert + key in one file).
cert.pkcs12Passphrase: Passphrase for the PKCS12 file (if any)
cert.installDescription: Replaces the currently running certificate with the one prepared above, and reloads Caddy. Irreversible without a fresh backup of the current certificate — confirm with your own password.
cert.installStarted: Installation started — check that the site still responds over HTTPS in a moment.
serial.heading: Serial number setup
serial.description: Controls which number the next added movie gets, and the step used for numbering future movies. To change a specific movie's serial number, do it in that movie's edit window in the library instead.
serial.adminOnly: Only administrators can change this setup.
serial.reuseFreedHint: When on, a new movie/show automatically gets the lowest free (freed) number in its series before the counter advances. A number is freed when an entry is deleted or moved to the shopping list. Note: only gaps between the lowest and highest used number are reused.
serial.renumberDigitalHint: One-time action: gives every existing digital movie/show a new, contiguous D# number starting from 1, in the order they were created. Fixes a historical side effect of an earlier migration, where digital entries kept an inherited number instead of starting over. Never touches physical (M#/T#) numbers. Cannot be undone.
serial.confirmRenumberDigital: This gives ALL existing digital movies/shows a new D# number starting from 1. Physical (M#/T#) numbers are not touched. This action cannot be undone — continue?
deleted.heading: Deleted movies
deleted.description: When a movie is deleted, it is logged here along with its serial number — the number is then free to be reused by a new movie.
deleted.none: No movies have been deleted yet.
sys.heading: System settings
sys.description: External API keys and the Plex integration. Can be set via .env on the server instead — a value set here overrides that, immediately, without a restart. Keys are never shown again once saved, only whether a key is set and from where. The Plex server URL is the exception — it is not a secret, and is therefore shown with its actual value.
sys.groupBarcodeDescription: Used to guess a title from a scanned barcode, before the actual TMDb search. The primary source is tried first, the others as fallback afterwards.
sys.groupEmailDescription: Outbound email for messages in the portal (e.g. a wish being approved or moved to the library), to users who have set their email in Settings → Account.
sys.plexServerUrlHint: Not a secret — shown as-is, e.g. http://192.168.1.50:32400
sys.anthemHostHint: Not a secret — shown as-is, e.g. 192.168.1.60. Used by the diagnostics page under Settings → Ops.
sys.anthemPortHint: Default is 14999 — Anthem's fixed network control port, normally not changed.
sys.emailFromAddressHint: Not a secret — shown as-is, e.g. "Voldby BIO <noreply@laces.dk>". No email is sent if either the key or this address is missing.
sys.primarySourceHint: tried first when scanning, the other three as fallbacks afterwards
plexDiag.heading: Plex connection (troubleshooting)
plexDiag.description: Tests the connection to Plex and shows how many of your movies and TV shows can be matched. Always fetches fresh, bypassing the cache, so a just-corrected URL or token is tried immediately. The badge on the cards is enabled per user under "Show fields" in Movies and TV Shows.
plexDiag.noSections: Plex responded, but no movie or TV libraries were found. Does the token's account have access to the libraries?
plexDiag.noTmdbGuids: Note: none of the items in Plex have a TMDb id. The sections are probably using an older agent — matching therefore falls back to title and year, which is less certain.
plexDiag.unmatchedHint: The first of your titles without a match. If they really are in Plex, it is usually because the title or year differs — compare with what Plex calls them.

plexImport.heading: Import from Plex
plexImport.description: Creates everything your Plex server has that the portal does not already have. Metadata comes from TMDb, not from Plex — so imported movies and shows look like everything else in the library. Media type is set to Digital, and the format is derived from the resolution in Plex (4K → D-4K, 1080 → D-1080, 720 → D-720, the rest → D-480). Anything you already have is skipped.
plexImport.tagHint: Applied to everything created, so you can filter the result in the library afterwards. Empty field = no tag. Also used by the automatic Plex scan below.

plexImport.unmatchedHint: Plex has no TMDb id for these, and searching on title and year did not give exactly one answer. They are not imported — add them manually via scan or TMDb search if you want them.
plexImport.failedHint: These were recognised but could not be created. Try the import again — it is usually a temporary TMDb error.
detail.classificationRequired: Media type and format must be chosen before this can be saved to the library. The media type decides which number series it gets — M#/T# for physical, D# for digital.
plexImport.formatFallback: resolution unknown in Plex — set to D-1080
plexAutoImport.heading: Automatic Plex scan
plexAutoImport.description: Automatically run the same import as the button above, at regular intervals — so new movies/shows added to Plex show up in the library on their own, without anyone having to remember to click "Import from Plex". The manual button stays available alongside it.
anthemDiag.heading: AVM 70 diagnostics
anthemDiag.description: Live monitoring of the Anthem AVM 70's input, volume, mute, audio mode and incoming audio format — to build up experience with the device's actual behavior and timing, before the real automation (e.g. start a movie in Plex → set audio mode → wait until stable → unmute) is built. Read-only — changes nothing on the AVM. Only one diagnostics session can run at a time.
